title: Longest Common Subsequence
description:
A subsequence keeps the order of characters but may skip some. Find the length of the longest subsequence that two strings have in common.

Input format
Line 1: the first string s.
Line 2: the second string t.
Both contain lowercase letters.

Output format
One integer: the length of the longest common subsequence.
hints: Compare the last characters of the two strings. What do you do if they are equal, and what if they are different?
Let dp[i][j] be the answer for the first i characters of s and the first j characters of t. If s[i-1] == t[j-1] then dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1, otherwise max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).
A subsequence may skip characters. Finding the longest common contiguous substring is a different (easier) problem and gives smaller answers.
